title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
description: Ten current Ohio University places for studying, gathering, recreation, art, and campus events.

cards.title: College Green
cards.subtitle: Historic campus green
cards.notes: Bring a blanket or meet classmates before a campus program; check the university calendar for current events scheduled on the green.
cards.short_summary: A central outdoor setting for university gatherings and performances.
cards.evidence_claim: Ohio University lists College Green as the site of the 2026 Involvement Fair and describes the Under the Elms concert series there.
cards.source_title: Center for Student Engagement & Leadership | Ohio University
cards.access_notes: Outdoor events and access vary by schedule and weather; consult the university calendar.

cards.title: Baker University Center Front Room
cards.subtitle: Baker University Center
cards.notes: Use the shared seating for a casual meet-up or a pause between classes; the stage may be reserved while the room remains open.
cards.short_summary: A public Baker Center room with seating and a reservable stage.
cards.evidence_claim: Ohio University states that the Front Room is open to the public even while events are taking place, with only its stage reservable.
cards.source_title: Baker University Center Event Spaces | Ohio University
cards.access_notes: The stage may be in use for a reservation; follow posted room and event guidance.

cards.title: Alden Library Learning Commons
cards.subtitle: Alden Library, second floor
cards.notes: Choose this floor when your group needs computers, group rooms, or multimedia tools; use the library’s room-reservation process when needed.
cards.short_summary: An active, technology-rich setting for collaborative academic work.
cards.evidence_claim: Ohio University Libraries identifies Alden's second-floor Learning Commons as an active, technology-rich study environment with group study rooms.
cards.source_title: Alden Library Floors | Ohio University Libraries
cards.access_notes: Study rooms and library services have their own availability and reservation rules.

cards.entity_name: Alden Library Very Quiet Study Area
cards.title: Alden Library Very Quiet Study Area
cards.subtitle: Alden Library, fourth floor
cards.notes: Head here for focused individual work near the College Green entrance; keep conversation and audio low to match the designated setting.
cards.short_summary: A designated quiet option within Alden's fourth-floor study spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: Ohio University Libraries lists a Very Quiet Study Area among the study spaces on Alden Library's fourth floor.
cards.source_title: Alden Library Floors | Ohio University Libraries
cards.access_notes: Observe library noise guidelines and check current building access before visiting.

cards.title: Alden Library Seventh Floor
cards.subtitle: Alden Library, top floor
cards.notes: Take a focused reading or writing session to the top floor, where tables and the quieter setting support longer independent work blocks.
cards.short_summary: A top-floor quiet-study space with campus-facing views.
cards.evidence_claim: Ohio University Libraries says Alden's seventh floor is a popular quiet-study space with views overlooking campus.
cards.source_title: Alden Library Floors | Ohio University Libraries
cards.access_notes: Observe library noise guidelines and check current building access before visiting.

cards.title: Charles J. Ping Recreation Center
cards.subtitle: 82 South Green Drive
cards.notes: Plan an active break around the climbing wall, courts, track, or fitness areas; bring a physical OHIO ID for activity-area entry.
cards.short_summary: A three-floor campus recreation facility with courts, track, climbing, and fitness space.
cards.evidence_claim: Ohio University describes the Ping Center as a three-floor recreation facility with a climbing wall, courts, track, weight areas, and fitness rooms.
cards.source_title: Charles J. Ping Recreation Center | Ohio University
cards.access_notes: A valid physical OHIO ID is required for activity areas; hours and membership eligibility vary.

cards.title: Well-Being Wing
cards.subtitle: Ping Recreation Center, second floor
cards.notes: Use the studio for small-group connection or reserve a room for an approved gathering; ask staff about current wellness-suite access.
cards.short_summary: A Ping Center wellness area supporting individual and small-group connection.
cards.evidence_claim: Ohio University says the Well-Being Wing includes a studio for small-group programming and one-on-one connections, plus reservable rooms.
cards.access_notes: Located in Room 226 and nearby rooms on Ping's second floor; it follows Ping Center hours and reservation rules.

cards.title: Kennedy Museum of Art
cards.subtitle: Lin Hall, Ridges Green
cards.notes: Pair an exhibition visit with a walk around the Ridges; review gallery hours before leaving campus because the museum has seasonal schedules.
cards.short_summary: An academic art museum with exhibitions and collection-based learning.
cards.evidence_claim: Ohio University identifies the Kennedy Museum of Art as an academic museum offering exhibitions, programs, and learning opportunities for students and visitors.
cards.source_title: Plan Your Visit | Kennedy Museum of Art at OHIO
cards.access_notes: At 100 Ridges Circle in Lin Hall; verify seasonal gallery hours before visiting.

cards.title: Ridges Outdoor Museum
cards.subtitle: The Ridges trail system
cards.notes: Follow the outdoor learning route at your own pace and use the web-based tour materials to connect trail stops with campus research.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor learning experience built around Ridges trails and points of interest.
cards.evidence_claim: Ohio University describes the Outdoor Museum as an integrated outdoor learning experience across the Ridges trail network and regional points of interest.
cards.access_notes: Use marked trails and appropriate footwear; conditions and tour materials may change seasonally.

cards.title: Hockhocking Adena Bikeway
cards.subtitle: University-maintained section along the Hocking River
cards.notes: Use the paved path for a walk, run, or ride, and note the painted mile markers when planning a turnaround or meeting point.
cards.short_summary: A paved river corridor that links Athens with nearby communities and recreation.
cards.evidence_claim: Ohio University describes the Hockhocking Adena Bikeway as a 22-plus-mile paved path and says it stewards the segment between O'Bleness Hospital and Stimson Avenue.
cards.source_title: Sustainable Living Hub: Transportation | Ohio University
cards.access_notes: Use normal path safety practices; consult local notices for weather, maintenance, or route conditions.
